macro.label: VIX: 14.81
macro.text: S&P 500 at 7,650.50. The VIX closed below the prior Friday's 15.84 after touching 18.94 on Fed day. Strikes now pay less than before the decision; take the thinner premium rather than moving the strike closer to make it up.

macro.label: 10-Year Treasury Yield: about 5%
macro.text: Crossed 5% last week for the first time since July 2007, eased Thursday, and was back near 5% by Friday. Banks and other rate-sensitive names moved hardest on the swing.

macro.label: Thursday: Trump-Xi summit
macro.text: Trade and chip exports are on the table. A single headline can push a stock past its strike overnight, so names exposed to the outcome wait for Friday.

macro.label: Unscheduled oil risk
macro.text: Reports that more strikes on Iran are under consideration mean oil, already near $100 a barrel, can move on any day this week.

days.rule: No new positions from this slate. Nothing scheduled sits between Monday's window and Wednesday's Fed speeches.

days.rule: The week's first Fed speeches and the weekly oil report are out by 8:00 AM Pacific. These two financial-sector puts wait for both, since bank shares move hardest on the day's rate tone.

days.rule: No new positions today. Trump and Xi meet with trade and chip exports on the table, and one headline can gap a stock past its strike before the close.
